name: Conventional Deadlift
cues: Stand with the bar over your midfoot and grip just outside your legs
Pull the slack out and brace with a flat back before the bar moves
Squeeze your armpits to keep the bar against your legs
Push the floor away, then drive your hips through
Hinge first on the way down, then bend your knees once the bar passes them

qa.note: Family review 2026-10-01 rated needs work. review: Reads as a pull from the floor: plates on the floor, knees extend first and the hips drive after the bar passes them, hands closed on the bar. But the start is high-hipped with a flat back (hips ~120 deg, knees 59, trunk only ~15 deg above horizontal). That is forced by bar over midfoot, shoulders over the bar and the bar on the shins with this tall, short-armed figure, and needs the FLOOR_START_TOL soft-tissue override (worst case at the belly -69.7 mm vs a 72 mm tolerance). The owner should judge whether the flat back reads as a stiff-leg pull. | skeptic: Liftoff looks like a stiff-leg start, not a conventional deadlift. In figure-508-side.png at t=0.500 and 0.625 the top of the hips is level with or above the shoulders, and the trunk is about 10 to 20 deg above horizontal (pelvis.tilt 67.6 + lumbar 5 + thorax 6, which is about 79 deg from vertical). Knees are only at 59 deg and the shins are almost vertical (ankle_df max 3.5 deg in 508.qa.json). The coaching standard is hips above the knees and below the shoulders, with the knees forward over the bar. The accepted FLOOR_START_TOL lead decision covers the soft-tissue tolerances and the ~120 deg hip angle, not this. The result is visibly wrong for the record's cues ('Push the floor away, then drive your hips through'), and a first-time user would copy a high-hip start. | skeptic: Reads as a floor pull, with plates on the floor at t=0.5 to 0.625 and the right hand closed on the bar (refute-visual-foot/figure-508-foot_R.png t=0.5). The start is very high-hipped and flat-backed: in refute-visual-side/figure-508-side.png t=0.5 the trunk is almost horizontal and the shins nearly vertical, so at 480 px it looks close to a stiff-leg deadlift. It depends on the applied FLOOR_START_TOL lead decision, so the owner should judge it. No visible penetration.
